import type { Order } from './orders.ts'; /** * The component this fixture exists to blame. * * The bug: the filtered-and-sorted view of the orders is derived in the render * body, so it is recomputed from scratch on every keystroke, and the comparator * is `localeCompare` — correct for names with diacritics and roughly two orders * of magnitude slower than a plain comparison. Sorting ten thousand rows takes * about 133,000 comparisons, each constructing a collator, and all of it lands * inside the frame that is also trying to show the user the character they just * typed. * * It is a realistic bug rather than a contrived one: every part of it is a * defensible local decision. Derive in render rather than cache a stale value; * sort by name because the table is sorted by name; use `localeCompare` because * `<` gets the diacritics wrong. The cost only appears when they combine. * * Only the first page of rows is rendered. The fixture has to jank for exactly * one reason, and committing ten thousand rows would add a second, larger cost * that attribution could hide behind. */ /** How many of the sorted rows are actually rendered. */ const PAGE_SIZE = 50; export interface OrderTableProps { readonly orders: readonly Order[]; readonly query: string; } export function OrderTable({ orders, query }: OrderTableProps) { // @ground-truth: the two lines below are the fixture's known culprit. const visible = orders .filter((order) => order.customer.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase())) .sort((a, b) => a.customer.localeCompare(b.customer)); return ( {visible.slice(0, PAGE_SIZE).map((order) => ( ))}
Reference Customer Status Total
{order.reference} {order.customer} {order.status} {order.total.toFixed(2)}
{visible.length} of {orders.length} orders
); }
